property_summary: Only the contract owner can successfully call withdrawAll (calls by non-owners revert).
If the caller is not the contract owner, calling withdrawAll must revert.

Rule: withdrawAll always routes through the internal withdraw(path) so that a failing external recipient does NOT cause the owner's withdrawal to revert; the mutant that transfers directly to msg.sender can revert when msg.sender's fallback/receive reverts, breaking this property for some caller behavior.

For any caller and any contract balance, calling withdrawAll on the correct contract always succeeds (does not revert) because it routes through withdraw which sends to msg.sender via transfer from within that function call path; the mutant that transfers directly can revert for some malicious msg.sender (a revert-on-receive) causing withdrawAll to fail — so the reference always returns/does not revert while the mutant can revert for some counterparty behavior.

For any depositor amount and any owner address with arbitrary behavior, calling withdrawAll on the reference C always succeeds (does not revert) and empties the contract balance to 0; the mutant that transfers directly to msg.sender can revert when msg.sender's receive/fallback reverts, breaking this guarantee for some owner behavior.

For any owner address that accepts Ether (i.e., has a payable receive), withdrawAll always empties the contract balance (address(c).balance == 0) after it returns; the mutant that transfers directly can fail to empty the balance when the owner's payable fallback reverts or behaves adversarially, so there exist inputs (an adversarial owner contract) where withdrawAll does not leave c's balance at 0.

For any owner contract that REVERTS when receiving Ether, the reference C's withdrawAll still does not revert (because it calls withdraw which uses transfer from a different stack frame) while the mutant that transfers directly to msg.sender can revert; thus the reference always returns (call succeeds) when msg.sender is a reverting contract, but the mutant may revert for some such msg.sender.

After depositing some ether to the contract, owner withdrawAll always makes the owner's address balance increase by exactly the contract balance before withdrawal (i.e., withdraw transfers full amount rather than silently failing).
Calling withdraw by the owner never reverts for any requested value (withdraw always succeeds).
On the original contract P, calling withdraw(value) does not revert (i.e., withdraw always succeeds).
